notes: Chunk core, 36 files. Known-ledger entries (open) for these files were not re-reported. Go rule groups are N/A (empty hits) for the non-Go files (acdsl/*.md, *.json, *.acdsl, testdata).

findings.claim: New LoadFragment returns errors without the Component.Method prefix: fmt.Errorf("reading %s: %w") at 218 and fmt.Errorf("parsing %s: %w") at 222, so a malformed fragment surfaces as 'parsing /path: ...' with no LoadFragment: origin, unlike McpServer/Settings.get in the same file.
findings.evidence: Re-read internal/config/config.go 210-225 at the pinned head: both error constructors in the new function carry no prefix. Distinct from known code-style-NIT-70 (body duplication of Load); the prefix rule is violated in the new declaration regardless of whether it is folded into Load.
findings.fix: Prefix both messages: fmt.Errorf("LoadFragment: Failed to read %s: %w", ...) and fmt.Errorf("LoadFragment: Failed to parse %s: %w", ...).

findings.claim: The new nested-run scan nests its success path under `if err == nil {` (251) and then range → if inside it, three control levels where the guide asks new code to stay at two and never nest the success path after an error check.
findings.evidence: Re-read internal/evals/evals.go 248-264: `nestedEntries, err := os.ReadDir(skillRoot); if err == nil { for ... { if ... continue } ... } }`. The flat loop above (236-246) is written flat; only the new block nests. Known code-style-NIT-78 covers the duplicated loop body, NIT-8 the in-function regexp compile; neither names the success-path nesting.
findings.fix: Extract the nested scan into loadNestedEvalDirs(dir, skill string) ([]EvalDir, []string) that returns early on the ReadDir error, and append its result in LoadForSkill.

findings.claim: The new package-level function validateScopeName is inserted inside Store's method block, between (*Store).InvocationsBySkill and (*Store).SentimentByBatch, instead of with the free functions after the type blocks.
findings.evidence: Re-read internal/sessions/sessions.go 205-251: InvocationsBySkill (Store method) at 208, validateScopeName (free func, new) at 223, collectInvocations (free func, pre-existing) at 232, SentimentByBatch (Store method) at 251. The pre-existing collectInvocations placement is legacy; the new declaration chose the same misplacement.
findings.fix: Move validateScopeName below the last Store method (Scopes), in the unexported free-function group.

findings.claim: TestFingerprint defines its own `run` git closure (288-292) that duplicates the `run` closure inside gitRepoWithAgentWorktrees (262-266) in the same file, differing only by the -c user.* flags.
findings.evidence: Re-read internal/repos/registry_test.go 259-307: both closures build append([]string{"-C", repo, ...}, args...), call exec.Command("git", ...).CombinedOutput() and require.NoError(t, err, string(output)). TestFingerprint is new in this diff.
findings.fix: Extract one file-level helper runGit(t *testing.T, repo string, args ...string) (always passing the -c user.* flags) and call it from both gitRepoWithAgentWorktrees and TestFingerprint.

findings.claim: TestLoadPolicy's failure cases (unknown-mode 117-121, malformed-json 124-128) and the absent-file case omit meta and input fields (_expected, _shouldPass, _taskExempt, content), relying on zero values, while the guide requires every meta field set explicitly in pass/fail tables and the sibling tables in this diff (TestExpandInstallMarkers installEnv: "", TestDetectContextCoverage _shouldPass: false) set them.
findings.evidence: Re-read internal/acdsl/policy_test.go 74-146: case literals at 117 and 124 carry only _id and content; the outcome (_shouldPass false) is implicit. Known code-style-NIT-68 covers the conditional t.Run body and NIT-12 the field names; neither covers the omitted meta fields.
findings.fix: Set every field in each case literal, e.g. unknown-mode: _expected: "", _shouldPass: false, _taskExempt: false, absent: false, content: `{"mode": "loose"}`.

findings.claim: The edited SyncAll doc comment was not reflowed: line 17 reads only `// Called once at` and the sentence continues on line 18, leaving a ragged two-word line in the middle of the godoc paragraph.
findings.evidence: Re-read internal/routines/bootstrap_darwin.go 13-22 at the pinned head: line 16 ends a sentence, line 17 is `// Called once at`, line 18 starts `// server startup: ...`. The diff inserted three lines before the original `Called once at` wrap point without rewrapping.
findings.fix: Rewrap lines 16-19 so `Called once at server startup: ...` continues on full-width comment lines.

findings.claim: The Windows SyncAll doc comment still states `unregistered -> register+enable (routine arrived via git pull)` unconditionally, but the new branch at 157-160 skips an unregistered (NotFound) routine carrying the default-disabled marker; the darwin twin's comment was updated for the same change, this one was not.
findings.evidence: Re-read internal/routines/sched_windows.go 135-171: comment 135-139 lists three reconcile arms, none mentioning default-disabled; code 157 `if state == "NotFound" && routine.DefaultDisabled { ... continue }`. bootstrap_darwin.go 14-16 documents the marker.
findings.fix: Amend the comment: `unregistered -> register+enable (routine arrived via git pull), unless it carries a default-disabled marker;`.
